results.summary: This project is a work-in-progress design intended to drive a seven-segment display, with eight outputs mapped to the segment lines A through H. The documentation is essentially empty, consisting only of placeholders such as 'WIP' and 'TODO', so the actual functionality cannot be determined. No testing procedure or external hardware requirements are described. The design is notable only for being an incomplete template.

This project appears to be a test design with eight inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation is largely nonsensical and incomplete. The only concrete information is a truth table that defines the expected output for each input combination, suggesting a combinational logic function. No external hardware or testing procedure is described beyond checking outputs against the truth table. The design is notable only as a poorly documented test structure.

This project implements a full adder built from a half-adder and a full-adder, with two inputs and one output. The documentation includes a complete truth table for testing the adder's behavior. No external hardware is required beyond the standard Tiny Tapeout setup. The design is notable as a fundamental building block for arithmetic circuits.

This project is a decimal counter that counts from 0 to 9 continuously when enabled, with outputs intended for a seven-segment display. The counter uses BCD encoding and is designed for educational purposes. It is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested by observing the display output. The design is notable for its simple counting functionality.

This project is a full adder circuit with three inputs and two outputs, implementing binary addition. The documentation provides a truth table for verification. No external hardware is required beyond the standard Tiny Tapeout setup. The design is notable as a fundamental arithmetic building block.

This project is a placeholder with no meaningful documentation, consisting only of TODO notes. The pins include two inputs and one output, but the functionality is described only as 'TODO'. No testing procedure or external hardware requirements are described. The design is notable only for being an incomplete placeholder.

This design implements a multiplexer that selects between two inputs based on a clock signal, with the selected output on one pin and copies of the inputs on two other pins. The documentation describes it as a workshop result and mentions a seven-segment display in the one-line description, though the display is not directly used in the described logic. The design is a basic combinational circuit. It is notable for being a simple educational example.

This project is a very basic circuit that switches the output number from 0 to 1 on a seven-segment display, as described. It has two inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation states it is only for pipeline testing and advises against using it. The design is a simple combinational circuit. It is notable only for its minimal functionality.

This project is a test design with eight inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation explicitly states that it does not work and cannot be tested. The design is non-functional and serves only as a placeholder or failed experiment. No external hardware or testing procedure is described. The design is notable only for being a non-functional test structure.

This project is a factory test structure with eight inputs and eight outputs, designed to verify chip functionality. The documentation describes a truth table for testing, but the design is incomplete and not intended for end users. No external hardware is required beyond the standard Tiny Tapeout setup. The design is notable for its test-oriented purpose.
